notes.summary: Reconstructs intrinsic primary boundaries, normalization fibers, and completion invariance on all semivaluations. Only the infinite-conductor stratum is closed.
notes.detailedSummary: For positive-dimensional reduced excellent local rings, proves compact primary sections, exact gauge changes, finite-normalization surjectivity and conductor-controlled fibers, retaining nonminimal supports. For every Noetherian local ring, proves the completion homeomorphism and exact contraction/extension of primary ideals. Nilpotents and the empty zero-dimensional boundary are treated explicitly.
notes.text:
Let (R,m) be a positive-dimensional reduced excellent Noetherian local ring. Semivaluations take values in [0,∞], satisfy multiplicativity and the ultrametric inequality, and have 0<v(m)<∞. Their support is prime and strictly smaller than m. Ideal values are minima on finite generating sets; expressing generators in terms of another generating set proves independence.

For a proper m-primary ideal a, write V_a={v:v(a)=1}. The semivaluation axioms define a closed subset of the compact Hausdorff product [0,∞]^R: extended addition and minimum are continuous, and the order relation is closed. The equation v(m)=1 is closed. If m^r⊂a⊂m^s, then s v(m)≤v(a)≤r v(m). Rescaling therefore identifies V_a with V_m and proves compactness. Every primary ideal value is positive, finite, continuous and bounded on V_a. For another primary b, the exact section change is H_ab(v)=v/v(b); its denominator and reciprocal are bounded. Its inverse and cocycle follow directly from homogeneity. The sections represent the same intrinsic centered ray boundary.

Nonemptiness follows by choosing p such that R/p is a one-dimensional local domain. Excellence gives finite normalization, and a local factor above its closed point is a DVR. Pulling back its order and rescaling gives a boundary point. The background used here is the Nagata consequence of excellence and the DVR characterization of one-dimensional normal Noetherian local domains; no resolution is assumed.

A nilpotent n has infinite value. Applying the ultrametric inequality in both directions gives v(f+n)=v(f), so reduction preserves the boundary and all ideal gauges. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field and has empty centered boundary. All function classes on that empty boundary are the singleton empty function.

Let S be the finite normalization in the total quotient ring and c=Ann_R(S/R). The conductor is also an S-ideal, cS=c, and R=S×_(S/c)(R/c): an element of S with residue coming from R differs from an element of R by an element of c⊂R. Let W be the semivaluations on S with w(aS)=1. A semivaluation on a finite product selects one primitive idempotent with value zero and annihilates the others. Thus W is the finite disjoint union over normal components. Its finitely many local-center pieces above m are clopen, using Chinese remainder elements that are zero at one center and one at the others. Localization preserves values because the denominators are units. The same closed-product argument proves compactness of W.

Restriction ρ:W→V_a is surjective. Indeed, for v with support p, lying over supplies P⊂S above p, and L=Frac(S/P) is finite over K=Frac(R/p). Let A⊂K be the valuation ring of v. The integral closure of A in L has a prime above its maximal ideal. A valuation ring of L dominates the resulting local domain. Here the dominating-valuation existence lemma can be proved by Zorn on dominating local subrings: if neither x nor x⁻¹ belongs to a maximal such subring, at least one adjoining extension has proper extension of its maximal ideal and can be localized to a larger dominating ring. If both extended ideals were the whole ring, their polynomial relations for 1 would make both x and x⁻¹ integral. The resulting finite algebra would equal its maximal-ideal multiple, contradicting Nakayama. This proves the valuation-ring property.

The extension intersects K in A, since an element outside A has inverse in its maximal ideal. Every new value γ is torsion modulo the old value group: in a polynomial equation for an element of L at least two terms attain the least value, so (i−j)γ is an old value. Dividing its old real value by i−j defines a well-defined order-preserving real extension; common multiples prove independence and additivity. Integral elements have nonnegative value, since otherwise their monic equation has a uniquely smallest leading term. Restoring P with infinite value gives the required semivaluation lift. This does not assume separability or defectlessness.

Consequently ρ is a compact-to-Hausdorff quotient. If v(c)<∞, choose c₀∈c of finite value. Every lift is uniquely determined by w(s)=v(c₀s)−v(c₀); the subtracted term is finite. If v(c)=∞, lifts annihilate c, and equality of restrictions is exactly equality through S/c→R/c. Z={w:w(c)=∞} is CLOSED; its finite-value complement is OPEN and need not be closed. A finite continuous function on W descends continuously precisely when it is fiber constant. This is a topological statement, not a positivity theorem. These rules commute with primary gauge changes.

Completion requires neither excellence nor normality. For any Noetherian local R, restriction V_(aRhat)(Rhat)→V_a(R) is a homeomorphism. Fix v and d=v(m)>0. For F∈Rhat choose F_N∈R representing it modulo m^N. For M≥N, v(F_M−F_N)≥Nd. Once v(F_N)<Nd occurs, all subsequent values stabilize; otherwise the values tend to infinity. The limit defines vhat(F), independently of representatives, and min(vhat(F),Nd)=min(v(F_N),Nd). Representatives of sums and products prove the axioms, including infinite values. Units have value zero, and finite generators preserve normalization. Every extension satisfies these truncation identities, proving uniqueness.

For continuity use q(t)=t/(1+t), q(∞)=1. On V_a, d≥1/r, and q(min(v(F_N),Nv(m))) approximates q(vhat(F)) uniformly with error at most 1/(1+N/r). Thus all extended coordinates are continuous; restriction is visibly continuous.

Every proper primary J⊂Rhat is extended from J∩R: choose N with m^N Rhat⊂J and lift generators modulo that power through R/m^N≅Rhat/m^N Rhat. The lifts and m^N generate J. The same quotient argument proves contraction of a primary extension is the original ideal. Ideal values agree on every semivaluation. Unit ideals give zero separately. Uniform closures and decreasing completions are therefore preserved, without an equivalence claim for all model categories.

The complete expanded proof is in n1.md, argument.md and P12.2-paper.tex. Rerun document generation with python3 make_delivery.py. Input identities are retained in reports/input-hashes.json. These are mathematical drafts using the stated algebraic background, not correctness grants from hashes or execution.

notes.summary: Independent numerical Cartier positivity on actual primary blowups has exactly the primary-ideal uniform closure, including nonnormal models and arbitrary characteristic. Raw and decreasing classes remain distinct.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs directed models, actual Cartier effectivity, finite evaluation at nonminimal supports, continuity, and uniform approximation from below. The section correction uses T=H0(Y,OY), c0=m^(h+1), and c0T⊂m. Proves exact gauge/completion rules and forward geometric normalization. Does not identify raw cones before closure or arbitrary singular weak-Weil limits.
notes.text:
Use the boundary of n1. Admissible models are actual Y_I=Bl_I Spec R for proper primary I. Their Rees algebras embed in R[t], so the models are reduced, projective and isomorphisms off m. The tautological ideal is invertible and locally generated by a regular element: I O_Y=O_Y(−E_I), with E_I effective and −E_I relatively ample.

Exceptional integral Cartier divisors include their trivialization off the closed fiber. Real Cartier divisors are finite real combinations. On nonnormal models, effectivity means the cone generated by ACTUAL effective integral Cartier divisors with this trivialization, rather than nonnegative Weil coefficients. Require −D in that cone. Independently, numerical nefness requires nonnegative degree on every proper integral contracted curve. Let M_a consist of these nonpositive Cartier evaluations, including zero; define C_a^geom as their uniform closure.

The model system is directed. On Y_(IJ), the product of the pulled-back ideals is generated locally by a regular f. Put J′=f⁻¹J in the total quotient ring. Then IJ′=A. An expression 1=Σx_l y_l gives a dual basis for I, because y_l I⊂A. Thus I is finite projective of generic rank one, hence locally rank one; likewise J. Primary ideals contain regular elements by avoidance of the finitely many minimal primes. The blowup universal property gives domination of Y_I and Y_J. Generic components are preserved, so Cartier pullbacks are legitimate. On a contracted curve the pullback degree is zero for point image, or its positive generic degree times the degree on its curve image. Numerical nefness and actual effectivity are preserved.

For any exceptional integral F on Y_I there is N with −NE_I≤F≤NE_I in actual Cartier order. The coherent fractional sheaves O(F)+O_Y and O(−F)+O_Y, modulo O_Y, are supported on the closed fiber. A power of I annihilates them, by Noetherianity and a finite affine cover; the resulting inclusions prove the bounds. Thus E_I is an order unit on every fixed finite real Cartier span.

For v with support p, use the valuation ring of Frac(R/p). Its generic point maps to Y_I off the closed fiber, and properness extends this map uniquely. Pull back O(F), retaining its generic trivialization. This is a rank-one lattice with nonzero generator of finite value. Define f_F as the negative value of that generator. Units do not change it. For effective E, this gives the positive value of a generator of O(−E). The order bounds give |f_F(v)|≤Nv(I). Evaluation is additive, homogeneous and unchanged on dominating models; it never subtracts two infinite values. Extend it linearly to real divisors.

The precise geometric background is proper coherence over a Noetherian affine base, ample twisting/global generation, ample openness in a finite real Cartier span, and nef plus a positive ample perturbation on a projective scheme over a field. All contracted curves lie in the projective closed fiber. That fiber may be nonreduced: integral curves and degree tests are on its reduction, and ampleness is invariant under Noetherian nilpotent thickening. Fiber ampleness gives relative ampleness over a neighborhood; a neighborhood of the closed point of a local spectrum is the whole spectrum. These applications require neither normality nor residue characteristic zero, and introduce no resolution or SNC premise.

Set T=H0(Y_I,O_Y). Proper coherence makes it a finite R-algebra. Restriction off the closed fiber embeds R⊂T and identifies them away from m. Hence m^h kills T/R for some h. Choose c0=m^(h+1), giving c0T⊂m as actual elements of R. This is the algebra of the PRIMARY MODEL, not the full normalization.

For a rational negative exceptional L with O(L) relatively ample, sufficiently divisible large k makes O(kL) globally generated. Its finite section module F_k⊂T exists because negative effectivity gives O(kL)⊂O_Y. J_k=c0F_k is an R-ideal, proper because c0T⊂m, and primary because it is the unit ideal off m. Its extension is (c0O_Y)O(kL). Global generation at the valuation-ring center supplies a unit coefficient among its generating sections. Therefore, on ALL semivaluations,

−v(J_k)/k=f_L−v(c0)/k.

The ideal c0O_Y need not be invertible; only its finite ideal value is used. For arbitrary integral F choose N with L=F−NE_I negative and relatively ample. For one suitable k this gives f_F=−v(J_k)/k+Nv(I)+v(c0)/k. Thus every Cartier evaluation is continuous and bounded, without assuming continuity of lifted centers. Real evaluation retains these properties.

For negative real numerical-nef D and ε>0 choose δ>0 with δ||v(I)||∞<ε/3. D−δE_I is ample. Write D=−Σd_j A_j with d_j≥0 and actual effective integral Cartier A_j. Round d_j upward to sufficiently close nonnegative rationals and choose rational δ′ close to δ with δ′>δ/2. Ample openness and finite-span continuity retain ampleness and make the uniform change less than ε/3. The resulting rational D′ is ACTUALLY negative, satisfies D′≤D−(δ/2)E_I, and has negative integral divisible multiples even on nonnormal models. The section construction, with k large enough that ||v(c0)||∞/k<ε/3, gives g_k=−v(J_k)/k≤f_D and ||f_D−g_k||∞<ε.

Conversely −t v(J) is the evaluation of −tE_J on its actual primary blowup, and is nef because the tautological bundle is generated. Consequently C_a^geom equals the uniform closure C_a of zero and scaled proper-primary ideal functions. Finite real nonnegative combinations have the same closure: rationally approximate their scales and express the common-denominator sum as one scaled product-ideal function. Ideal sums give maxima at common rational scales; uniform approximation extends this to real scales. C_a is a closed convex cone of continuous nonpositive functions, stable under finite maxima.

For the exact conventions, P_a is the finite nonnegative real cone of positive gauges v(I) for ideals containing a boundary power, including the unit ideal. Such ideals are unit or proper primary. Q_a=−P_a has uniform closure C_a, and Q_a⊂M_a by adding pulled-back negative nef divisors on a common primary model. Reverse raw equality is not claimed. Write N_R for the negative raw normalization-ideal convention: continuous downstairs functions whose pullbacks lie in the RAW corresponding cones on normal components. Ideal extension proves Q_R⊂N_R. General N_R⊂C_R requires n4's saturation test and is not presumed. Nor is all C_R claimed to belong to the raw normalization cone. The n5 example makes Q_R⊂N_R strict.

Define G_a as the nonbottom infima of nonempty decreasing nets in C_a, with an explicitly adjoined bottom −∞ giving Gbar_a. This is an additional completion accompanying the proved independent positivity comparison, not a singular weak-Weil classification. Exact gauge change is f_(D,b)(v/v(b))=f_(D,a)(v)/v(b). Bounded positive denominators preserve uniform closure and decreasing nets. Product directed sets prove Gbar is stable under nonnegative scaling, sums and finite maxima; zero times bottom is defined as zero. A sum of two nonbottom functions may be bottom on a reducible germ, which is why bottom is retained. Completion invariance follows from n1 and the comparison, not model-category equivalence.

On each local normalization branch, the blowup of the extended primary ideal maps to the downstairs blowup. The degree argument preserves positivity, and evaluation is exactly restriction. Thus normalization pullback embeds C_R into C_S and Gbar_R into Gbar_S; it is injective and uniformly isometric on continuous functions by n1's surjectivity. Every image function is fiber constant, including on the infinite-conductor stratum. Reverse membership is not inferred from topological descent.

Expanded arguments are in n2.md and P12.2-paper.tex; hypotheses and exclusions are in source-application-ledger.md. Rerun python3 make_delivery.py. The supplied model proposals are provenance, not supports.

notes.summary: The nonbottom decreasing geometric completion recovers the FULL published smooth BFJ formal class on all semivaluations, with zero/unit, bottom and dimension-one qualifications.
notes.detailedSummary: At smooth closed points over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, applies the completely read BFJ immediate units at their actual hypotheses. Proves the continuous-class identification and the full decreasing-net identification using finite weak nef limits, minimal rational faces, and commuting all-retraction infima. Historical dependency editions are not claimed independently inspected.
notes.text:
This proof uses n1 and n2 and applies the published Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson paper, Valuations and Plurisubharmonic Singularities, Publ. RIMS 44 (2008), 449–494. Its Sections 1–4 setting is a smooth closed point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, localized at that point. Smooth complex germs are included. No singular, nonnormal or positive-characteristic extension of these source theorems is made.

The exact source definitions are Definition 2.1, the weakly closed nef Weil cone generated by ideal divisors; Definition 2.5, finite strong-continuous quasimonomial functions with nef divisorial Weil data; and Definition 2.8, canonical extension by the infimum of ALL retractions. Proposition 3.11 supplies the unique finite continuous convex extension on each CLOSED dual-complex face. Proposition 3.14 supplies C_v g(v_m)≤g(v)≤g(v_m) for quasimonomial v and implies g(v_m)<0 for nonzero formal g. Proposition 2.7 and Definition 2.8 extend the upper bound to all semivaluations. These published units, rather than proposal labels, are the inputs.

For primary I, a smooth principalization gives a negative generated numerical-nef ideal divisor. Proposition 2.2 identifies it with source nefness, and Proposition 1.14 identifies the continuous evaluation with −v(I). This evaluation is the canonical extension: the principalized ideal is an exceptional monomial times a unit, so its value and its value at every sufficiently high retraction are the same combination of exceptional values. Proposition 2.7 then identifies the infimum of all retractions with the actual ideal value, including nonzero supports. Zero is separately formal.

The literal proper-primary wording of Proposition 3.13 needs a zero correction. Its complete proof constructs

A_j=L²(2^j g)+mhat^(4^j),
g_j=−2^(−j)v(A_j)=max(h_j,−2^j),
h_j=2^(−j)log|L²(2^j g)|.

Theorems 3.9 and 3.10 give the multiplier estimate and subadditivity, so these functions decrease to g on the quasimonomial locus. For g=0, Definition 3.6 gives L²(0)=Rhat, and A_j is UNIT. A decreasing family of strictly negative proper-primary functions cannot converge to zero, so zero is retained separately.

For g≠0 put c=g(v_m)<0. Theorem 3.9 gives h_j(v_m)≤c+A(v_m)/2^j<0 eventually. The multiplier ideals are therefore eventually proper; adding mhat^(4^j) makes A_j proper primary. Discard the finite initial unit terms. For arbitrary non-quasimonomial v and t>g(v), Definition 2.8 supplies π with g(r_π(v))<t. For late j, g_j(r_π(v))<t, while g(v)≤g_j(v)≤g_j(r_π(v)). Hence the same sequence decreases to g on ALL semivaluations, including points where g(v)=−∞. By n1 these completed primary ideals contract exactly to primary ideals downstairs.

Every globally continuous formal g belongs to C_m: use this repaired sequence and Dini on the compact section, treating zero separately. Conversely suppose h_l=−t_l v(I_l), allowing zero models, converge uniformly to finite continuous h. Their divisorial coefficients give a finite weak Weil limit W; finite-coordinate trace compatibility is preserved, and the published weak closed nef cone makes W nef. Proposition 3.11 supplies H_W. On each closed simplex, h and H_W agree on dense rational divisorial points and hence everywhere by continuity. Each h_l satisfies its canonical retraction formula. Infima of two families differing uniformly by ε differ by at most ε, so uniform convergence yields

h(v)=inf_π h(r_π(v))=H_W(v).

Thus C_m is exactly the globally continuous BFJ class, not every bounded upper semicontinuous formal function.

Now let h_i decrease in C_m and let g=inf_i h_i be nonbottom. If inf_i h_i(v_m)=−∞, the all-semivaluation upper bound forces g to be bottom. Therefore g(v_m) is finite. The published Izumi bound makes g finite at every quasimonomial point. Its divisorial coefficients give a finite weak nef Weil limit W, and Proposition 3.11 supplies H_W on closed faces.

On each rational closed simplex, g is finite convex, by passing the convexity inequality through the decreasing limit. A finite convex function is continuous on its relative interior. For any point take its MINIMAL rational face. Its relative interior has dense rational divisorial points, where g=H_W. Continuity identifies the functions on that relative interior. Applying the argument separately to every lower-dimensional face includes every boundary point; boundary continuity is obtained through identification with the published H_W, rather than falsely deduced from interior convexity alone.

Finally,

g(v)=inf_i inf_π h_i(r_π(v))=inf_π inf_i h_i(r_π(v))=inf_π g(r_π(v)).

These infima commute as infima over a product index set, even with extended values. This is exactly Definition 2.8, so g=H_W on the ENTIRE boundary. Conversely the repaired Proposition 3.13 supplies decreasing continuous approximants to every nonzero formal function, and zero has its constant net. Therefore G_m=BFJ_full, while Gbar_m=BFJ_full∪{−∞}. Bottom is obtained by −Nv(m) but is excluded from the ordinary formal class, which is finite on the quasimonomial locus. Other primary gauges follow by n2's exact positive denominator rule.

Dimension one is checked independently. For a smooth DVR with parameter z and a=(z^d), the section is the single valuation ord_z/d. The blowup of (z^N) is the identity; its closed-point divisor is Cartier and there are no contracted integral curves. Negative real closed-point divisors give all finite nonpositive constants, and decreasing completion adds bottom. This is the one-dimensional formal interpretation, without importing the higher-dimensional exceptional-model discussion.

The frozen BFJ PDF SHA-256 is 26d2d8dd2546efd55a148b4ff233892e88cfeab6c34de7fa613a7ad2e543d7f8; text SHA-256 is 9a72054bc227fca9231feb65ec631e6b4a91e68c10307d38fa5c23d5965de93f. Complete immediate units and context were displayed at frozen LF 340–355, 390–835, 895–1021, 1022–1234 and 1235–1410. Printed pages 468–479 were directly extracted from the PDF and the essential definitions/approximation units re-read. Published theorem application is distinguished from proving or inspecting historical resolution, Izumi and multiplier-ideal editions. BdFFU Proposition 2.4(b) is not used.

Files n3.md, source-application-ledger.md and reports/bfj-pages-468-479.txt retain expanded proofs and provenance. Rerun python3 inspect_inputs.py for extraction and python3 make_delivery.py for the paper.

notes.summary: New general continuous conductor image theorem: canonical saturation ideals reduce uniform geometric descent to convergence on the closed infinite-conductor stratum.
notes.detailedSummary: For every finite continuous normalization-side geometric function, defines explicit downstairs saturation ideals. Their dyadic normalized gauges decrease and converge correctly off the infinite-conductor stratum. Correct convergence on that closed stratum is equivalent to uniform convergence and membership in the downstairs continuous geometric image. Automatic sufficiency of fiber constancy and unbounded completed-image compatibility remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Use R⊂S, V, W, ρ and Z={w:w(c)=∞} from n1, and the geometric continuous classes from n2. Let C_S be the finite product of the classes on local normalization branches with common gauge aS. Equivalently it is the uniform closure of finite negative real ideal combinations on semilocal S, with ideals containing a boundary power and allowed to be unit on some branches. Indeed such ideals are determined in the Artinian quotient S/a^N S; its product decomposition glues ideals at the finitely many centers. Extending each branch ideal by units elsewhere realizes arbitrary finite tuples, followed by uniform limits.

For any h∈C_S put A=−h≥0, finite continuous on W. No fiber-constancy assumption is imposed. Define

I_k(A)={r∈R: w(r)≥kA(w) for every w∈W},
B_k(w)=w(I_k(A))/k.

Semivaluation inequalities make I_k an ideal; Noetherianity makes it finitely generated. If M=||A||∞, it contains a^(ceil(kM)+1), since the boundary gauge is one. Hence it is unit or proper primary and B_k is finite continuous. Its generators satisfy the defining inequalities, so B_k≥A. Multiplication gives I_kI_l⊂I_(k+l), hence B_(2k)≤B_k. Thus B_(2^j) decreases and is bounded above by B_1.

For ε>0 there are an S-ideal J containing a boundary power and integer l>0 with A≤w(J)/l≤A+ε uniformly. To obtain them, approximate h by finite real negative ideal combinations, rationally approximate their scales, combine them as a common-denominator product ideal, and add a sufficiently small rational boundary gauge to move the positive approximation above A. The common gauge is identically one, so the shift is an arbitrarily small constant.

Put q=ceil(k/l). The R-ideal cJ^q⊂R is contained in I_k(A), because all its elements have value at least q w(J)≥kA. At finite-conductor points,

A(w)≤B_k(w)≤q w(J)/k+w(c)/k.

Product ideal values add: multiply minimizing generators, which remains valid with nonminimal support. Sending k→∞ and then ε→0 proves B_(2^j)(w)→A(w) on W\Z. This is a POINTWISE correction and makes no uniform claim about w(c)/k.

The following conditions are equivalent: (i) h∈ρ*C_R; (ii) B_(2^j)(w)→A(w) at every w∈Z; (iii) B_(2^j)→A uniformly on W.

For (ii)⇒(iii), convergence off Z was just proved. The continuous nonnegative errors B_(2^j)−A decrease to zero on compact W. For each ε their sublevel open sets form an increasing cover; compactness supplies one index covering W. This is the full Dini argument. Each −B_(2^j) is a pullback of a downstairs unit-or-primary ideal model. Pullback is an isometry on continuous functions because ρ is surjective. Uniform convergence therefore gives a downstairs uniform limit in C_R, establishing (i). Fiber constancy is obtained from this conclusion rather than presumed sufficient.

For (i)⇒(iii), approximate the downstairs function from below by −v(K)/l, with K downstairs unit-or-primary and uniform error ε, using the same rational-product/boundary-shift construction. Then w(K)≥lA and K^ceil(k/l)⊂I_k(A). Consequently

A≤B_k≤ceil(k/l)w(K)/k≤A+ε+||w(K)||∞/k.

This proves uniform convergence for all k. Finally (iii)⇒(ii) is immediate. Thus the canonical DYADIC saturation sequence tests the exact continuous geometric image for every finite continuous h upstairs.

This theorem handles arbitrary nonprimary conductors with infinite values. When Z is empty its condition is vacuous and C_R pulls back onto all C_S, recovering isolated finite-birational continuous descent as a consequence. It does not establish that the test is automatic for every fiber-constant h.

There is an exact conductor-quotient form. Put Ibar_k=(I_k+c)/c⊂R/c. At w∈Z, w(I_k)=wbar(Ibar_k), where wbar is restriction through S/c. This value is finite because I_k contains a boundary power. The test is precisely inf_j 2^(−j)wbar(Ibar_(2^j))=A(w) for w∈Z. These quotient ideals retain the GLOBAL saturation constraints; replacing them by quotient-only saturations is not justified.

The construction is gauge invariant: extend A homogeneously to the centered cone and both sides of every membership inequality scale equally. I_k is unchanged by primary section changes; its gauges and errors acquire the same bounded positive denominator. Uniform convergence and the closed-stratum test are preserved.

No effective finite algorithm for the universal saturation ideals is asserted. A general unbounded decreasing limit need not have finite continuous A, so this argument does not apply Dini to it. An approximation-compatible conductor image theorem for the completed class remains unresolved.

The complete proof is in n4.md, argument.md and P12.2-paper.tex. Rerun python3 make_delivery.py. No supplied conductor proposal or historical annotation is a correctness support.

notes.summary: New non-isolated cusp-surface example separates the entire downstairs finite real raw ideal cone from a normalization profile, while explicit primary ideals give uniform geometric descent with error at most 2/k.
notes.detailedSummary: For the excellent characteristic-zero domain R=k[t²,t³,z] at its origin, proves normalization S=k[t,z], conductor t²S and singleton boundary fibers. For J=(z+t,t²), explicit downstairs primary K_k satisfy k w(J)≤w(K_k)≤k w(J)+2 on every semivaluation. A Taylor argument excludes every finite real positive combination of downstairs primary gauges. This obstructs raw equality, not continuous or completed geometric descent.
notes.text:
Let k be a characteristic-zero field and R=k[t²,t³,z]_(t²,t³,z)⊂S=k[t,z]_(t,z), with m=(t²,t³,z). This is an excellent local domain. S is its normalization: t is integral, S is finite with module generators 1,t, the fraction fields agree, and S is normal. Any element of the common fraction field integral over R is integral over S and belongs to S. The finite algebra has the unique maximal ideal above m, giving the indicated localization.

The conductor is c=t²S. Before localization, elements of R have zero coefficient of t¹, with coefficients in k[z]; modulo t²S their image is k[z]. Multiplication by t in S/t²S shows that an element of R is in the conductor exactly when its constant-in-t coefficient vanishes. This proves the conductor formula, also after localization. Its support is the positive-dimensional z-axis. R/c=k[z]_(z), while S/c=k[z,t]_(z,t)/(t²). Semivaluations kill the nilpotent t, so these quotient valuation spaces coincide. By n1 normalization fibers are singletons both on and off the conductor. Thus ρ is a boundary homeomorphism despite nonnormality.

On the m-section write s=w(t), u=w(z). Both are positive, possibly infinite separately, with min(2s,u)=1. The conductor stratum is s=∞, u=1. The finite-conductor monomial points s=N,u=1 converge to it on every localized polynomial. Hence the finite-value complement is not closed, and w(c)/k=2s/k cannot be a uniformly vanishing correction.

Take b=z+t and the normalization primary ideal J=(b,t²). Its positive gauge A(w)=min(w(b),2s) is finite continuous and fiber constant. Its negative belongs to the raw normalization-ideal convention and to C_S.

For each integer k≥1 set

F_k=b^k(z−kt), G_k=t²b^k, H_k=t^(2k+2), K_k=(F_k,G_k,H_k)⊂R.

The t-linear coefficient of F_k is kz^k−kz^k=0; all its higher t-powers belong to R. The other generators are in the conductor. They are proper, and their common zero in S is only the origin: H_k forces t=0 and then F_k=z^(k+1). Integral lying over proves K_k is downstairs primary.

Every generator has value at least kA: their values are k w(b)+w(z−kt), k w(b)+2s, and (k+1)2s. All summands are nonnegative, with infinity permitted. The upper bound w(K_k)≤kA+2 holds on EVERY semivaluation as follows.

The proved draft progress is substantial: n1 reconstructs intrinsic boundaries, conductor fibers and completion; n2 gives resolution-free independent numerical Cartier positivity on actual primary blowups and its exact uniform ideal comparison, gauges and forward normalization; n3 identifies the nonbottom decreasing class with the FULL published smooth BFJ formal class on ALL semivaluations, treating zero/unit, bottom and dimension one; n4 supplies an exact general continuous conductor image criterion; n5 gives a non-isolated excellent cusp surface separating the entire raw finite real cone while proving explicit uniform geometric descent with error ≤2/k.
